name: Pimoroni RGB Encoder Breakout
description: Rotary encoder with an RGB LED inside its clear shaft, read over I2C: a Nuvoton MS51 microcontroller running Pimoroni's IO Expander firmware counts the encoder in hardware (an 8-bit wrapping count in register 0x06, chip ID 0xE26A in 0xFA/0xFB) and drives the red, green and blue LEDs with its PWM unit. No push switch. No regulator: the MS51 runs from the 3-5V pin (2.4-5.5 V) and the 10 kOhm SDA/SCL/INT pull-ups go to that supply, so power it from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board. I2C address 0x0F (changeable in software, kept in flash). Sold as: Pimoroni RGB Encoder Breakout (PIM522), 5-pin 0.1" header 3-5V, SDA, SCL, INT, GND (Raspberry Pi pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9).
eli5: A knob you can spin round and round forever, with a coloured light inside it. A tiny chip counts the clicks and tells your board over two wires, and your board can tell it what colour to glow.

pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V (MS51 2.4-5.5 V, no regulator; the I2C/INT pull-ups go to this pin, so use 3.3 V with a 3.3 V board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output from the MS51 (P0.0 once the firmware's INT pin swap is set), low when the count has changed until the flag is cleared; 10 kOhm pull-up to the supply. Not needed for basic use (poll the count instead)

buildNotes: Header order 3-5V, SDA, SCL, INT, GND matches Raspberry Pi pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, so it can sit straight on a Pi.
Power it from 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico/Pi: there is no regulator and the 10 kOhm SDA/SCL/INT pull-ups go to the supply pin, so 5 V would put 5 V on the I2C lines.
Check the chip ID first: registers 0xFA (low) and 0xFB (high) read 0xE26A.

The firmware only counts after setup: encoder pins 12 (A, P0.5) and 3 (B, P1.2) as pulled-up Schmitt inputs, pin 11 (C, P0.6) as an open-drain low output, ENC_1_CFG 0x05 = 0x3C, then set bit 0 of ENC_EN 0x04.
The count register 0x06 is 8 bits and wraps; the driver keeps a running total, so read it at least every ~64 steps of turning.
LED: red PWM5 (pin 1), green PWM1 (pin 7), blue PWM2 (pin 2), inverted PWM outputs; set the duty registers then the LOAD bit (PWMCON0 0x98 bit 6), which the MS51 clears when done.
No push switch on this encoder.

driver.code:
# Pimoroni RGB Encoder Breakout (PIM522), MicroPython driver.
# A Nuvoton MS51 microcontroller running Pimoroni's IO Expander ("ioe") firmware reads the rotary
# encoder in hardware and drives the RGB LED inside the knob with its PWM unit. The firmware maps
# the MS51's special-function registers into an I2C register space (address 0x0F by default).
# Sequences follow Pimoroni's own libraries (ioe-python ioexpander/__init__.py and
# pimoroni-pico drivers/ioexpander + libraries/breakout_encoder).
#
# Board wiring of the MS51 (IOE pin numbers): LED red = pin 1 (P1.5, PWM5), green = pin 7
# (P1.1, PWM1), blue = pin 2 (P1.0, PWM2); encoder A = pin 12 (P0.5), B = pin 3 (P1.2),
# common C = pin 11 (P0.6, driven low as open drain). INT is on P0.0 (INT pin swap bit).
import time

ADDR = 0x0F
CHIP_ID = 0xE26A

# ioe firmware registers
_CHIP_ID_L = 0xFA
_CHIP_ID_H = 0xFB
_VERSION = 0xFC
_ADDR = 0xFD
_CTRL = 0xFE
_INT = 0xF9            # bit0 TRIGD (interrupt flag), bit1 OUT_EN, bit2 PIN_SWAP (0 = P1.3, 1 = P0.0)
_ENC_EN = 0x04         # bit0 enable channel 1, bit1 count microsteps on channel 1
_ENC_1_CFG = 0x05      # pin A | pin B << 4
_ENC_1_COUNT = 0x06    # 8-bit count, wraps (two's complement)
# MS51 SFRs as mapped by the firmware
_P0 = 0x40             # bit-addressed: write 0b1000|bit to set, bit to clear
_P1 = 0x50
_P0M1 = 0x71
_P0M2 = 0x72
_P1M1 = 0x73
_P1M2 = 0x74
_P0S = 0xC2
_P1S = 0xC4
_PIOCON0 = 0x9E
_PIOCON1 = 0xC9
_PNP = 0x96
_PWMCON0 = 0x98        # bit7 PWMRUN, bit6 LOAD (clears itself), bit4 CLRPWM
_PWMCON1 = 0x9F        # bits 2:0 clock divider
_PWMPL = 0x99
_PWMPH = 0x91
_BIT_ADDRESSED = (_P0, _P1)

# (port P reg, M1, M2, S reg, bit) per pin, and (piocon reg, bit, PWM L reg, PWM H reg) for PWM pins
_ENC_A = (_P0, _P0M1, _P0M2, _P0S, 5, (_PIOCON1, 2))   # IOE pin 12
_ENC_B = (_P1, _P1M1, _P1M2, _P1S, 2, (_PIOCON0, 0))   # IOE pin 3
_ENC_C = (_P0, _P0M1, _P0M2, _P0S, 6, None)            # IOE pin 11 (ADC-only pin, no PWM)
_LED_R = (_P1, _P1M1, _P1M2, _P1S, 5, (_PIOCON1, 5), 0xCB, 0xC8)  # pin 1, PWM5
_LED_G = (_P1, _P1M1, _P1M2, _P1S, 1, (_PIOCON0, 1), 0x9B, 0x93)  # pin 7, PWM1
_LED_B = (_P1, _P1M1, _P1M2, _P1S, 0, (_PIOCON0, 2), 0x9C, 0x94)  # pin 2, PWM2

_MODE_PU = 0b10000   # input with pull-up (quasi-bidirectional, initial high)
_MODE_OD = 0b00011   # open-drain output
_MODE_PWM = 0b00101  # PWM, push-pull


class RGBEncoder:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR, brightness=1.0, timeout_ms=1000):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.timeout_ms = timeout_ms
        self._last = 0
        self._offset = 0
        self.direction = 1   # 1 = as counted by the chip, -1 = reversed
        cid = self.chip_id()
        if cid != CHIP_ID:
            raise OSError('RGB Encoder not found at 0x%02X (chip ID 0x%04X, expected 0x%04X)' % (addr, cid, CHIP_ID))
        # Encoder: A and B inputs with pull-ups and Schmitt triggers, C driven low.
        self._set_mode(_ENC_A, _MODE_PU, schmitt=True)
        self._set_mode(_ENC_B, _MODE_PU, schmitt=True)
        self._set_mode(_ENC_C, _MODE_OD)
        self._w8(_ENC_C[0], _ENC_C[4])                 # clear the bit: output low
        self._w8(_ENC_1_CFG, 12 | (3 << 4))            # channel 1 = pins 12 (A) and 3 (B)
        self._clr_bit(_ENC_EN, 1)                      # count whole steps, not microsteps
        self._set_bit(_ENC_EN, 0)                      # enable channel 1
        self.clear()
        # LED: PWM period gives 0-255 steps at the chosen brightness, divider 2.
        self.set_brightness(brightness)
        self._w8(_PWMCON1, 0b001)
        for led in (_LED_R, _LED_G, _LED_B):
            self._set_mode(led, _MODE_PWM, invert=True)

    # --- low level
    def _r8(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _w8(self, reg, v):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([v & 0xFF]))

    def _set_bit(self, reg, bit):
        if reg in _BIT_ADDRESSED:
            self._w8(reg, 0b1000 | bit)
        else:
            self._w8(reg, self._r8(reg) | (1 << bit))

    def _clr_bit(self, reg, bit):
        if reg in _BIT_ADDRESSED:
            self._w8(reg, bit)
        else:
            self._w8(reg, self._r8(reg) & ~(1 << bit))

    def _change_bit(self, reg, bit, state):
        if state:
            self._set_bit(reg, bit)
        else:
            self._clr_bit(reg, bit)

    def _set_mode(self, pin, mode, schmitt=False, invert=False):
        p, m1, m2, ps, bit, pio = pin[0], pin[1], pin[2], pin[3], pin[4], pin[5]
        gpio_mode = mode & 0b11
        initial = mode >> 4
        if mode == _MODE_PWM:
            self._set_bit(pio[0], pio[1])                # route the PWM channel to the pin
            self._change_bit(_PNP, pio[1], invert)       # output polarity
            self._set_bit(_PWMCON0, 7)                   # PWMRUN
        elif pio is not None:
            self._clr_bit(pio[0], pio[1])
        pm1 = self._r8(m1) & ~(1 << bit) & 0xFF
        pm2 = self._r8(m2) & ~(1 << bit) & 0xFF
        pm1 |= (gpio_mode >> 1) << bit
        pm2 |= (gpio_mode & 1) << bit
        self._w8(m1, pm1)
        self._w8(m2, pm2)
        if mode == _MODE_PU:
            self._change_bit(ps, bit, schmitt)
        self._w8(p, (initial << 3) | bit)

    def _pwm_load(self):
        self._set_bit(_PWMCON0, 6)                       # LOAD: latch period and duties
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while self._r8(_PWMCON0) & 0x40:
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > self.timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('timed out waiting for PWM load')
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    # --- identity
    def chip_id(self):
        return self._r8(_CHIP_ID_L) | (self._r8(_CHIP_ID_H) << 8)

    def version(self):
        return self._r8(_VERSION)

    # --- encoder
    def read(self):
        """Steps turned since clear(). The chip keeps an 8-bit count; wraps are tracked here,
        so call this at least once per ~64 steps of turning."""
        v = self._r8(_ENC_1_COUNT)
        if v & 0x80:
            v -= 256
        if self._last > 64 and v < -64:
            self._offset += 256
        if self._last < -64 and v > 64:
            self._offset -= 256
        self._last = v
        self.clear_interrupt()
        return (self._offset + v) * self.direction

    def clear(self):
        self._w8(_ENC_1_COUNT, 0)
        self._last = 0
        self._offset = 0

    # --- interrupt flag (set by the firmware when the count changes)
    def changed(self):
        return bool(self._r8(_INT) & 0x01)

    def clear_interrupt(self):
        self._clr_bit(_INT, 0)

    def enable_interrupt_out(self):
        """Drive the board's INT pin (active low). The breakout's INT is on P0.0, so PIN_SWAP is set."""
        self._set_bit(_INT, 1)
        self._set_bit(_INT, 2)

    # --- RGB LED
    def set_brightness(self, brightness):
        brightness = min(max(brightness, 0.01), 1.0)
        period = int(255 / brightness)
        self._w8(_PWMPL, period & 0xFF)
        self._w8(_PWMPH, period >> 8)
        self._pwm_load()

    def set_led(self, r, g, b):
        for led, v in ((_LED_R, r), (_LED_G, g), (_LED_B, b)):
            v = max(0, min(255, int(v)))
            self._w8(led[6], v & 0xFF)
            self._w8(led[7], v >> 8)
        self._pwm_load()

    # --- address (kept in the MS51's flash)
    def set_address(self, new_addr):
        self._set_bit(_CTRL, 4)
        self._w8(_ADDR, new_addr)
        self.addr = new_addr
        time.sleep_ms(250)
        self._clr_bit(_CTRL, 4)

from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pimoroni_rgb_encoder import RGBEncoder

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
enc = RGBEncoder(i2c)
print('chip ok, firmware v%d' % enc.version())
enc.set_led(0, 0, 64)
while True:
    n = enc.read()
    if n >= 0:
        enc.set_led(0, 64, 0)
    else:
        enc.set_led(64, 0, 0)
    print('count=%d' % n)
    time.sleep_ms(200)

# Pimoroni RGB Encoder Breakout (PIM522)

## Overview
A continuous-rotation rotary encoder (24 detents, no push switch) with a red/green/blue LED shining through its clear shaft, read over I2C. A **Nuvoton MS51** microcontroller running Pimoroni's **IO Expander ("ioe") firmware** counts the encoder in hardware and drives the three LED colours with its PWM unit, so your board only needs SDA and SCL. It is the same firmware as Pimoroni's IO Expander breakout, so the chip's pins have to be set up over I2C before it counts.

## Pinout (5-pin header, as printed)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| 3-5V | Supply, 3-5 V (MS51 2.4-5.5 V, no regulator) |
| SDA | I2C data (10 k pull-up to 3-5V) |
| SCL | I2C clock (10 k pull-up to 3-5V) |
| INT | Interrupt output, low when the count changed (optional) |
| GND | Ground |

The order matches Raspberry Pi header pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (3V3, SDA, SCL, GPIO4, GND), so the board can plug straight onto a Pi with the supplied right-angle socket.

## Electrical limits
- Supply 3-5 V on the board (MS51: 2.4-5.5 V). There is **no regulator**: the SDA/SCL/INT pull-ups go to the supply pin, so on a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico, Pi) feed it **3.3 V**.
- Current: a few mA plus up to roughly 20 mA with the LED fully on.
- I2C 100/400 kHz.

## Interface details (I2C address 0x0F)
| Reg | Content |
|---|---|
| 0xFA / 0xFB | Chip ID low / high = 0x6A / 0xE2 (0xE26A) |
| 0xFC | Firmware version |
| 0x04 | ENC_EN: bit 0 enable channel 1, bit 1 count microsteps |
| 0x05 | ENC_1_CFG: pin A | pin B << 4 (0x3C for this board) |
| 0x06 | ENC_1_COUNT: 8-bit two's-complement count, wraps |
| 0xF9 | INT: bit 0 flag (count changed), bit 1 drive INT pin, bit 2 INT on P0.0 |
| 0x98 | PWMCON0: bit 7 PWMRUN, bit 6 LOAD (self-clearing) |
| 0x99 / 0x91 | PWM period low / high |
| 0xCB/0xC8, 0x9B/0x93, 0x9C/0x94 | Duty low/high for red (PWM5), green (PWM1), blue (PWM2) |
| 0xFD / 0xFE | I2C address (bit 4 of CTRL unlocks it; kept in flash) |

Board wiring of the MS51 (IOE pin numbers): encoder A = pin 12 (P0.5), B = pin 3 (P1.2), common C = pin 11 (P0.6, open-drain low); LED red = pin 1, green = pin 7, blue = pin 2 (inverted PWM).
Read a register: write its number, then read (repeated start, `readfrom_mem`). Write: register number then the value.

## Wiring
| Breakout | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-5V | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) | pin 1 |
| SDA | GPIO21 | GP4 | pin 3 |
| SCL | GPIO22 | GP5 | pin 5 |
| INT (optional) | any GPIO | any GP | pin 7 |
| GND | GND | GND | pin 9 |

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from pimoroni_rgb_encoder import RGBEncoder
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
enc = RGBEncoder(i2c)          # checks the chip ID, sets up the encoder and PWM
enc.set_led(0, 0, 255)         # blue
print(enc.read())              # steps since clear()
enc.clear()
enc.direction = -1             # reverse the counting direction
```

## Gotchas
- Nothing counts until the driver has configured the encoder pins and ENC_EN; a fresh chip reads 0 forever otherwise.
- The hardware count is only 8 bits. The driver extends it by watching for wraps, so poll `read()` at least every ~64 steps of fast turning.
- Changing the address with `set_address()` stores it in flash; note the new address or you will have to scan for it.
- There is no push switch on this encoder (the RGB Potentiometer breakout is the version with end stops).
- In the Sparkbench simulator the slider sets the count register; LED colours are accepted but not shown.

## Datasheet
- MS51 datasheet: https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0174/1800/files/DS_MS51_16KBFlash_Series_EN_Rev1.01.pdf
- MS51 technical reference: https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0174/1800/files/TRM_MS51_16KBFlash_Series_EN_Rev1.03.pdf
- Product page: https://shop.pimoroni.com/products/rgb-encoder-breakout
- Firmware register map / library: https://github.com/pimoroni/ioe-python
